supplements.name: Creatine
supplements.description: Naturally occurring compound that helps regenerate ATP for explosive energy. Most researched sports supplement.
supplements.benefits: Increases strength, power output, and muscle hydration. May support cognitive function.
supplements.warnings: Stay well hydrated. Some water retention initially is normal.

supplements.name: Whey Protein
supplements.description: Fast-absorbing protein derived from milk. Rich in leucine for muscle protein synthesis.
supplements.benefits: Supports muscle recovery and growth. Convenient way to meet daily protein targets.
supplements.warnings: Avoid if lactose intolerant. Check for added sugars in flavored versions.

supplements.name: Casein Protein
supplements.description: Slow-digesting protein from milk. Provides sustained amino acid release over several hours.
supplements.benefits: Ideal for overnight muscle recovery. Promotes satiety.
supplements.warnings: Avoid if lactose intolerant. May cause bloating in some individuals.

supplements.name: Multivitamin
supplements.description: Comprehensive blend of essential vitamins and minerals to fill nutritional gaps.
supplements.benefits: Covers micronutrient deficiencies. Supports overall health and immune function.
supplements.warnings: Take with food. Do not exceed recommended dose. May cause nausea on empty stomach.

supplements.name: Fish Oil
supplements.description: Source of omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA for cardiovascular and brain health.
supplements.benefits: Reduces inflammation, supports heart health, improves brain function.
supplements.warnings: Take with meals. High doses may increase bleeding risk. Check for mercury-free certification.

supplements.name: Omega-3
supplements.description: Synonymous with fish oil. May also come from algae (vegan source).
supplements.benefits: Anti-inflammatory, cardiovascular support, cognitive health.
supplements.warnings: Check EPA/DHA ratio. Algae-based may be lower in EPA.

supplements.name: Vitamin D
supplements.description: Fat-soluble vitamin essential for calcium absorption, bone health, and immune function.
supplements.benefits: Supports bone density, mood, immune system. Many people are deficient.
supplements.warnings: Take with fat-containing meal. Get blood levels tested. Toxicity possible at very high doses.

supplements.name: Magnesium
supplements.description: Essential mineral involved in 300+ enzymatic reactions. Glycinate and citrate forms are preferred.
supplements.benefits: Improves sleep quality, reduces muscle cramps, supports relaxation and recovery.
supplements.warnings: May cause loose stools at high doses (oxide form). Glycinate is gentler on stomach.

supplements.name: Zinc
supplements.description: Essential trace mineral crucial for immune function, testosterone production, and wound healing.
supplements.benefits: Supports immune health, hormone balance, and recovery.
supplements.warnings: Do not exceed 40mg/day. Take with food to avoid nausea. Can cause copper deficiency at high doses.

supplements.name: Iron
supplements.description: Essential mineral for oxygen transport in blood. Critical for athletes, especially menstruating women.
supplements.benefits: Prevents iron-deficiency anemia, improves energy and endurance.
supplements.warnings: Take on empty stomach with vitamin C. Avoid with calcium, coffee, tea. Can be dangerous if not deficient - get tested first.

supplements.name: Calcium
supplements.description: Most abundant mineral in the body. Essential for bone health, muscle contraction, and nerve function.
supplements.benefits: Supports bone density and dental health. Important for muscle function.
supplements.warnings: Split doses for better absorption. Do not take with iron or zinc. Excess may increase kidney stone risk.

supplements.name: BCAA
supplements.description: Branched-Chain Amino Acids (Leucine, Isoleucine, Valine). Popular intra-workout supplement.
supplements.benefits: May reduce muscle soreness and support recovery during fasted training.
supplements.warnings: Low evidence if protein intake is sufficient (1.6g/kg). May interfere with serotonin synthesis.

supplements.name: Glutamine
supplements.description: Most abundant amino acid in the body. Supports gut health and immune function.
supplements.benefits: May support gut lining integrity and immune function during intense training.
supplements.warnings: Limited evidence for muscle-building claims. Consider for gut health issues.

supplements.name: L-Carnitine
supplements.description: Amino acid derivative that transports fatty acids into mitochondria for energy production.
supplements.benefits: May support fat metabolism and exercise performance. Antioxidant properties.
supplements.warnings: Take on empty stomach for better absorption. May cause fishy body odor at high doses.

supplements.name: Taurine
supplements.description: Conditionally essential amino acid important for cardiovascular and neuromuscular function.
supplements.benefits: May improve exercise performance, reduce cramping, and support heart health.
supplements.warnings: Generally well tolerated. May interact with blood pressure medications.

supplements.name: Beta-Alanine
supplements.description: Amino acid that increases muscle carnosine levels, buffering lactic acid during intense exercise.
supplements.benefits: Improves endurance in high-intensity efforts lasting 1-4 minutes.
supplements.warnings: Tingling sensation (paresthesia) is normal and harmless. Split doses to minimize.

supplements.name: Caffeine
supplements.description: Most widely consumed psychoactive substance. Powerful ergogenic aid.
supplements.benefits: Increases alertness, focus, and exercise performance. Reduces perceived exertion.
supplements.warnings: Avoid after 2pm. Tolerance builds over time. Can cause anxiety and insomnia. Cycle off periodically.

supplements.name: Pre-Workout
supplements.description: Combination supplement typically containing caffeine, beta-alanine, citrulline, and other ingredients.
supplements.benefits: Convenient blend for energy, focus, and pump during workouts.
supplements.warnings: Check caffeine content. Do not stack with additional caffeine. Start with half scoop to assess tolerance.

supplements.name: Ashwagandha
supplements.description: Ayurvedic herb classified as an adaptogen. KSM-66 and Sensoril are standardized extracts.
supplements.benefits: Reduces cortisol and stress. May improve sleep, recovery, and testosterone in men.
supplements.warnings: May interact with thyroid medications. Avoid if autoimmune condition without consulting doctor.

supplements.name: Rhodiola
supplements.description: Adaptogenic herb used in traditional medicine for fatigue and mental performance.
supplements.benefits: Reduces mental and physical fatigue. May improve mood and cognitive function.
supplements.warnings: Take on empty stomach. May cause dizziness at high doses. Not for bedtime use.

supplements.name: Turmeric
supplements.description: Spice containing curcumin, a potent anti-inflammatory compound. Enhanced by piperine.
supplements.benefits: Powerful anti-inflammatory and antioxidant. Supports joint health and recovery.
supplements.warnings: Must take with black pepper (piperine) for absorption. May interact with blood thinners.

supplements.name: Glucosamine
supplements.description: Compound found naturally in cartilage. Widely used for joint health.
supplements.benefits: May reduce joint pain and slow cartilage degradation in osteoarthritis.
supplements.warnings: May take 4-8 weeks to see effects. Shellfish-derived may cause allergic reactions.

supplements.name: Coenzyme Q10
supplements.description: Antioxidant compound essential for cellular energy production (ATP).
supplements.benefits: Supports heart health, energy production, and antioxidant protection.
supplements.warnings: Take with fat meal. Ubiquinol form is more bioavailable than ubiquinone.

supplements.name: Probiotics
supplements.description: Beneficial bacteria that support gut microbiome diversity and digestive health.
supplements.benefits: Improves digestion, immune function, and may support mental health via gut-brain axis.
supplements.warnings: Refrigerate if required. Take on empty stomach. May cause initial bloating.

supplements.name: Vitamin B12
supplements.description: Water-soluble vitamin essential for nerve function and red blood cell formation.
supplements.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, nerve health. Essential for vegans/vegetarians.
supplements.warnings: Sublingual form absorbs best. Very safe even at high doses (excess excreted).

supplements.name: Vitamin C
supplements.description: Water-soluble antioxidant vitamin essential for immune function and collagen synthesis.
supplements.benefits: Boosts immune system, enhances iron absorption, supports skin health.
supplements.warnings: Split doses for better absorption. High doses may cause digestive upset.

supplements.name: Vitamin K2
supplements.description: Fat-soluble vitamin that directs calcium to bones and away from arteries. MK-7 form preferred.
supplements.benefits: Works synergistically with vitamin D for bone and cardiovascular health.
supplements.warnings: Avoid if on blood thinners (warfarin). MK-7 has longest half-life.

supplements.name: Potassium
supplements.description: Essential mineral and electrolyte for fluid balance, nerve signaling, and muscle contractions.
supplements.benefits: Supports blood pressure regulation and muscle function.
supplements.warnings: OTC supplements limited to 99mg due to safety concerns. Get rest from diet (bananas, potatoes).

supplements.name: HMB
supplements.description: Beta-hydroxy beta-methylbutyrate, a metabolite of leucine. Anti-catabolic supplement.
supplements.benefits: May reduce muscle breakdown during intense training. More effective for beginners.
supplements.warnings: Most effective in untrained individuals. Split into 1g doses 3x daily.

supplements.name: Melatonin
supplements.description: Hormone naturally produced by the pineal gland that regulates sleep-wake cycle.
supplements.benefits: Improves sleep onset and quality. Useful for jet lag.
supplements.warnings: Start with lowest dose (0.5-1mg). Take 30-60 min before bed. Do not drive after taking.

supplements.name: Collagen
supplements.description: Structural protein found in skin, bones, and connective tissue. Available as peptides.
supplements.benefits: Supports skin elasticity, joint health, and gut lining. Take with vitamin C for synthesis.
supplements.warnings: Takes 4-12 weeks to see results. Type I/III for skin, Type II for joints.

supplements.name: Citrulline Malate
supplements.description: Amino acid that converts to arginine, increasing nitric oxide production for improved blood flow.
supplements.benefits: Enhances pump, endurance, and recovery. Reduces muscle soreness.
supplements.warnings: Take 30-60 min before exercise. 2:1 citrulline-to-malate ratio is standard.

supplements.name: Alpha-GPC
supplements.description: Choline compound that crosses the blood-brain barrier. Precursor to acetylcholine.
supplements.benefits: May improve power output, cognitive function, and mind-muscle connection.
supplements.warnings: Take on empty stomach for best absorption. May cause headache in sensitive individuals.

supplements.name: N-Acetyl Cysteine
supplements.description: Antioxidant amino acid derivative. Precursor to glutathione, the body's master antioxidant.
supplements.benefits: Powerful antioxidant support, liver protection, respiratory health.
supplements.warnings: Take on empty stomach. May interact with nitroglycerin and blood thinners.

supplements.name: L-Theanine
supplements.description: Amino acid found in tea leaves. Promotes relaxation without drowsiness.
supplements.benefits: Reduces anxiety, improves focus when combined with caffeine. Promotes calm sleep.
supplements.warnings: Very safe. Synergistic with caffeine for focused energy (2:1 theanine to caffeine).

supplements.name: Psyllium Husk
supplements.description: Soluble fiber supplement derived from Plantago ovata seeds.
supplements.benefits: Supports digestive health, regularity, and cholesterol management.
supplements.warnings: Always take with plenty of water. May interfere with medication absorption - separate by 2 hours.

supplements.name: Eleuthero
supplements.description: Also called Siberian Ginseng. Adaptogenic herb used for energy and endurance.
supplements.benefits: May improve endurance, reduce fatigue, and enhance immune function.
supplements.warnings: May interact with blood pressure and diabetes medications. Not true ginseng.

interactions.description: Calcium significantly inhibits iron absorption when taken together. Can reduce iron absorption by up to 60%.
interactions.recommendation: Take iron at least 2 hours before or after calcium supplements.

interactions.description: Iron and zinc compete for the same absorption pathways (DMT1 transporter). High-dose iron can reduce zinc absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Separate by at least 2 hours. Take iron in the morning, zinc at night.

interactions.description: High-dose calcium (>800mg) can significantly reduce zinc absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Take zinc supplements at least 2 hours apart from calcium.

interactions.description: Caffeine can reduce iron absorption by up to 40% when consumed with iron supplements.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid coffee or tea within 1 hour of taking iron supplements.

interactions.description: Vitamin C dramatically increases non-heme iron absorption (by 2-6x). This is generally beneficial but risky for people with hemochromatosis.
interactions.recommendation: Take together to boost iron absorption. However, avoid if you have iron overload disorder.

interactions.description: Vitamin D enhances calcium absorption. This is a beneficial synergy, not a negative interaction.
interactions.recommendation: This is a beneficial combination. Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium more effectively.

interactions.description: High-dose fish oil can deplete vitamin E levels. Omega-3s are oxidized using vitamin E.
interactions.recommendation: If taking high-dose fish oil (>3g), consider supplementing with vitamin E (100-200 IU).

interactions.description: Some studies suggest caffeine may blunt creatine's performance benefits, though evidence is mixed.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid taking creatine directly with high-caffeine pre-workouts. Separate by 30-60 minutes.

interactions.description: No negative interaction. This is actually a beneficial combination for muscle recovery.
interactions.recommendation: Safe to combine. Whey protein can improve creatine uptake due to insulin response.

interactions.description: Ashwagandha may stimulate thyroid hormone production, potentially causing hyperthyroidism when combined with thyroid medication.
interactions.recommendation: Consult your doctor before combining. Monitor thyroid levels if using both.

interactions.description: Ashwagandha may enhance the effects of sedative medications (benzodiazepines, barbiturates) causing excessive drowsiness.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combining with sedatives without medical supervision. May cause excessive sedation.

interactions.description: Turmeric/curcumin has antiplatelet effects and can increase bleeding risk when combined with anticoagulant medications.
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine with warfarin, aspirin, or other blood thinners without doctor approval.

interactions.description: Thiazide diuretics increase calcium retention. Combined with vitamin D, this can lead to dangerously high calcium levels (hypercalcemia).
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood calcium levels if on thiazide diuretics and vitamin D supplements.

interactions.description: Vitamin K2 directly antagonizes warfarin's blood-thinning mechanism, potentially making the medication ineffective.
interactions.recommendation: Do NOT take vitamin K2 if on warfarin. Consult your cardiologist.

interactions.description: Magnesium can enhance the blood-pressure-lowering effects of antihypertensive medications, potentially causing hypotension.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure closely. May need medication dose adjustment.

interactions.description: Magnesium can bind to certain antibiotics (tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones) in the gut, reducing their absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Take antibiotics at least 2 hours before or 4-6 hours after magnesium.

interactions.description: Zinc can reduce absorption of quinolone and tetracycline antibiotics.
interactions.recommendation: Separate zinc and antibiotic doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.description: Calcium supplements can significantly reduce absorption of levothyroxine (Synthroid).
interactions.recommendation: Take thyroid medication at least 4 hours before calcium supplements.

interactions.description: Iron supplements can reduce absorption of levothyroxine.
interactions.recommendation: Separate iron and thyroid medication by at least 4 hours.

interactions.description: BCAAs (especially valine) may compete with L-DOPA for transport across the blood-brain barrier.
interactions.recommendation: If on L-DOPA medication, consult doctor before supplementing with BCAAs.

interactions.description: Antibiotics kill beneficial bacteria along with harmful ones, reducing probiotic effectiveness.
interactions.recommendation: Take probiotics at least 2 hours after antibiotics. Consider shelf-stable strains.

interactions.description: High-dose omega-3s (>3g) have mild antiplatelet effects that can increase bleeding risk with anticoagulants.
interactions.recommendation: Keep omega-3 dose under 3g if on blood thinners. Monitor for unusual bruising.

interactions.description: Grapefruit juice inhibits CYP3A4 enzyme, increasing statin levels to potentially dangerous concentrations.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid grapefruit juice with statin medications.

interactions.description: Combination of caffeine and ephedra (ma huang) has been linked to serious cardiovascular events including heart attacks and strokes.
interactions.recommendation: This combination is banned by the FDA. Never combine.

interactions.description: Both are stimulants. Combining can cause increased heart rate, jitteriness, and cardiac arrhythmias.
interactions.recommendation: Limit caffeine intake if using albuterol inhalers. Monitor heart rate.

interactions.description: Alcohol enhances melatonin's sedative effects, potentially causing excessive drowsiness and respiratory depression.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combining. Can cause dangerously deep sedation.

interactions.description: Orlistat (fat blocker) significantly reduces absorption of fat-soluble vitamins including vitamin D.
interactions.recommendation: Take vitamin D at least 2 hours apart from orlistat. May need higher dose.

interactions.description: Both have mild blood-thinning effects. Combination at normal doses is usually safe but may increase bleeding time.
interactions.recommendation: Generally safe at standard doses. Monitor for unusual bruising or bleeding.

interactions.description: CoQ10 may reduce the effectiveness of warfarin due to vitamin K-like activity.
interactions.recommendation: Consult doctor if on warfarin. May need INR monitoring.

interactions.description: High-dose zinc (>40mg/day) depletes copper by inducing metallothionein, which preferentially binds copper.
interactions.recommendation: If supplementing zinc >30mg daily, add 1-2mg copper supplement.

interactions.description: Psyllium can bind to medications in the gut and reduce their absorption significantly.
interactions.recommendation: Take all medications at least 2 hours before or after psyllium husk.

interactions.description: Glucosamine may enhance the anticoagulant effect of warfarin, increasing INR and bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely if taking glucosamine with warfarin. Consult doctor.

interactions.description: L-Carnitine may interfere with thyroid hormone action, potentially reducing effectiveness of thyroid medication.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by 2-4 hours. Monitor thyroid levels.

interactions.description: NAC combined with nitroglycerin can cause severe hypotension (dangerously low blood pressure) and headaches.
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine without medical supervision.

interactions.description: Vitamin C increases aluminum absorption from antacids, potentially harmful for kidney patients.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by 2 hours. Especially important for those with kidney disease.

interactions.description: Magnesium can reduce absorption of bisphosphonates (osteoporosis medications like alendronate).
interactions.recommendation: Take bisphosphonate first thing in morning, magnesium at bedtime.

interactions.description: Caffeine increases lithium excretion, potentially reducing its therapeutic effect.
interactions.recommendation: Maintain consistent caffeine intake while on lithium. Changes in caffeine can affect lithium levels.

interactions.description: Caffeine and theophylline are chemically similar. Caffeine can increase theophylline to toxic levels.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid or strictly limit caffeine if taking theophylline.

interactions.description: High-dose vitamin E (>400 IU) may increase bleeding risk when combined with anticoagulants.
interactions.recommendation: Keep vitamin E under 400 IU if on blood thinners.

interactions.description: Saw palmetto may have mild anticoagulant properties that can add to blood thinner effects.
interactions.recommendation: Consult doctor if on warfarin or other anticoagulants.

interactions.description: Both affect the HMG-CoA reductase pathway. Theoretical concern but no clinical significance at standard doses.
interactions.recommendation: Generally safe combination. No dosage adjustment needed.

interactions.description: Collagen supplements may theoretically affect platelet function. Very mild effect at standard doses.
interactions.recommendation: Usually safe. Inform your doctor if you take collagen supplements before surgery.

interactions.description: Live probiotic bacteria may cause infections in immunocompromised individuals.
interactions.recommendation: Do not use live probiotics if on immunosuppressant therapy without doctor approval.

interactions.description: Dairy products and antacids containing calcium significantly reduce non-heme iron absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Take iron with water and vitamin C, away from dairy and calcium-based antacids.

interactions.description: Ashwagandha may stimulate immune function, potentially counteracting immunosuppressive therapy.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid ashwagandha if on immunosuppressant medications.

interactions.description: Theoretical concern that glutamine may be converted to glutamate, potentially lowering seizure threshold.
interactions.recommendation: Consult neurologist if on anti-epileptic medications.

interactions.description: ACE inhibitors (lisinopril, enalapril) increase potassium levels. Supplementing potassium can cause hyperkalemia.
interactions.recommendation: Do not supplement potassium without doctor approval if on ACE inhibitors.

interactions.description: Angiotensin receptor blockers increase potassium retention. Additional supplementation risks hyperkalemia.
interactions.recommendation: Do not supplement potassium without doctor approval if on ARBs (losartan, valsartan).

interactions.description: Rhodiola may affect serotonin levels, potentially interacting with SSRIs and increasing risk of serotonin syndrome.
interactions.recommendation: Consult psychiatrist before combining with SSRI medications.

interactions.description: Turmeric may lower blood sugar, potentially causing hypoglycemia when combined with diabetes medications.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood sugar closely if combining turmeric with diabetes medication.

interactions.description: Citrulline increases nitric oxide, which lowers blood pressure. May cause additive hypotensive effect.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure. May need medication adjustment.
